designDecisionsMadeThisPass.decision: CoverageSource takes the LOCALITY SIGNAL (city/state/zip + raw query) as input, not a pre-resolved countyFips.
designDecisionsMadeThisPass.why: Building against CP2's own roster-endpoint recommendation surfaced a second gap CP2 did not hit: this repo has NO zip-to-county or city-to-county crosswalk anywhere (grepped artifacts/api-server/src/lib/ -- zero hits for zcta/tigerPlace/censusPlace/cityToCounty/zipToCounty). A roster-only endpoint would still leave this lane unable to ask 'is Killeen's county in the roster' without building a SECOND hand-maintained crosswalk -- the same anti-pattern one level down. Pushing county resolution server-side, into hauska-engine/retrieval-api (which already has direct Postgres access per CP2's own recommended query), avoids that. Full reasoning in the CONTRACT artifact.

designDecisionsMadeThisPass.decision: Three-state CoverageVerdict (covered / not-covered / indeterminate), never two.
designDecisionsMadeThisPass.why: Mirrors parcelRecordReaderClient.ts's existing undefined-vs-null split for the exact same reason: a consumer that cannot tell 'unknown' from 'yes' is a presence-shaped check (P-205 falsifier #3). not-covered requires countyFips+countyName+state together or the client itself downgrades it to indeterminate rather than serve an incomplete claim.

designDecisionsMadeThisPass.decision: The literal operator constraint is applied UNCONDITIONALLY: every zero-hit query with no confirmed coverage answer declines, including inside the six already-onboarded counties, not only for genuinely-new counties.
designDecisionsMadeThisPass.why: Considered and rejected a softer alternative (skip the whole mechanism when unconfigured, preserving today's no-hit until a real endpoint is wired) as inconsistent with the operator's literal words ('with no coverage source available, it MUST fail closed... never fall through to no-hit') and confirmed by concrete evidence that the existing test suite ALREADY encodes 'in-coverage no-match returns plain no-hit' as a hard invariant in three separate files -- meaning the fail-closed default's true blast radius (all six working counties, not just new ones) is real and had to be handled by updating those tests' assumptions explicitly, not by narrowing the constraint to dodge them. This is the single biggest interpretive call in this pass; flagged prominently in the close and to the operator directly, since it is reversible before deploy (merge only, no deploy) but not something to bury.

designDecisionsMadeThisPass.decision: Both new missClass tokens (coverage_check_unavailable, county_out_of_coverage) ship WITHOUT calling missClassDisplayText().
designDecisionsMadeThisPass.why: That function (tool-honesty.ts) THROWS on a token with no row in the shared @empressaio/atom-contract/display VOCABULARY, by explicit design ('a closed missClass with no display row is a defect in this package, not a value to paper over'). Neither token exists there yet and this lane does not own that package. Shipping unenriched matches the ALREADY-established precedent for no-hit and located-unbound ('ship unenriched, as they always have') rather than crashing find_parcel the first time either token fires. Declared, not silent: the CONTRACT artifact names the exact recommended vocabulary entries for whoever picks up that package.
